meeting_header:
Date: 2026-10-06
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 54 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recorder: Fireflies
Notes: Recorded with customer permission; redacted attachments to be shared via Trust Center link.
summary: High-level posture review of Bluehaven's SOC 2 / ISO27001 readiness for Redwood private deployment. Discussed Trust Center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO approach, audit log retention and KMS integration options. Agreed next steps for sharing reports, mapping controls, and scheduling a KMS deep-dive.
topics: Trust Center access & redacted SOC 2 Type II delivery
Controls mapping: customer matrix vs Redwood control set
Audit logs: retention, provenance, and export paths
Data residency (EU region requirement) and private deployment modes
Proof-of-concept timelines and pilot data flows
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got permission to record. Quick intro, I'm Maya from Redwood, AE. We've got Leo and Priya from our security/infra team.
[00:23] Samir: Hi all, Samir K., Head of Security at Bluehaven. We're mainly here to understand the compliance artifacts and how Trust Center access will work.
[01:05] Maya: Great, so agenda, high-level posture readout, show how you can access redacted SOC 2 artifacts, then map to your controls.
[01:35] Emma: Quick thing, we need EU data residency, plus we run some workloads on-prem. Is that supported in the private deployment?
[01:50] Leo: Yes, Private supports VPC and on-prem. There are a couple of options: full private control-plane or hybrid VPC peering. Performance/ops tradeoffs though.
[02:10] Carlos: If we go private, what about audit logs? We need 7 years retention and immutable logs for audits.
[02:30] Priya: We support exporting audit logs to your S3 or GCS bucket, can integrate with SIEMs. Retention is configurable but for long-term you may ship to your own cold storage. There are immutability flags you can manage.
[02:52] Samir: Are those logs encrypted with our KMS? We have a BYOK requirement.
[03:05] Leo: Short answer, yes. We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). The flow is in our docs but we'll walk it through. There's a nuance with some hosted fallbacks where keys have to be available across regions, we'll discuss.
[03:40] Maya: I'm going to drop the Trust Center link in the chat after the call; you'll get read-only access to redacted SOC2 Type II and ISO evidence bundles.
[03:55] Ruth: Legal wants to confirm redaction levels — no customer PII in the report.
[04:05] Maya: Understood, we redact downstream PII, the Type II has redactions, we'll flag any remaining specifics.
[04:28] Speaker 1: (mumble) ok, uh-- question on control mapping, do you have a template?
[04:45] Priya: Yes, we have a control mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to SOC2/ISO controls. We'll share that; it's been helpful to customers.
[05:15] Emma: On SSO, we're SAML based + SCIM for provisioning. How does user provisioning map to Redwood roles?
[05:30] Leo: We support SAML for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is role-based with admin/operator/auditor built-in, and you can create custom roles. SCIM will map groups to roles. There can be small sync delays during big org changes.
[06:10] Samir: We also want event-level audit for who called the API and token-level cost attribution — is that available?
[06:28] Priya: Token-level traces are in Console; request-level audit logs include API keys used, caller IPs and model called. The retention defaults are 90 days but we can export to your archive.
[06:50] Carlos: For ISO evidence, is there a separate bundle or is it the same artifacts as SOC2?
[07:05] Maya: There's overlap but we produce separate mappings. ISO will have some additional process docs. We'll include both in the shared Trust Center set.
[07:30] Emma: About data residency — if we pin region EU-west, will all inference traffic stay in region or are there control plane calls that go out of region?
[07:48] Leo: With Private, you can keep control plane and data plane in-region. With hosted, there's some control-plane metadata that might cross borders depending on region settings. We'll show architecture diagrams.
[08:20] Samir: If we do a Dedicated reserved instance, does the SLA cover log delivery and retention?
[08:36] Maya: SLAs focus on availability/latency. Log delivery SLAs can be part of an enterprise addendum; we can discuss in contracting.
[08:55] Emma: On KMS, supported key providers?
[09:05] Priya: AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault, and HSM integrations for on-prem. For cross-region replication with BYOK there are caveats, we'll document key rotation flows.
[09:40] Samir: We need proof-of-control for key access — like who can rotate keys and key policies, logs.
[09:55] Leo: Key usage logs are available in your KMS audit trail; Redwood does not have plaintext key access. We'll provide architecture docs that show separation of duties.
[10:20] Maya: Quick pause, is anyone blocked from viewing the Trust Center because of firewall? I'll follow up via email.
[10:35] Emma: We might need the link to be accessible from corporate network; often blocked by strict proxies.
[10:50] Maya: Noted. I'll send an alternate route if needed.
[11:12] Samir: For the controls mapping, we'll mark which require remediation vs compensating controls. How detailed is the mapping?
[11:30] Priya: It's pretty granular — control objective, Redwood control, evidence location, and suggested customer evidence. You can filter by control-owner and risk level.
[11:55] Carlos: Timeline: We're aiming for a vendor audit window in Q1 2027. Can we get everything prepped?
[12:10] Maya: Yes that's doable. Typical path: we share artifacts, you map controls, run a short pilot (logs + KMS), then we support evidence collection ahead of audit.
[12:32] Samir: One more — encryption in transit specifics? TLS versions?
[12:45] Leo: TLS 1.2 & 1.3, mutual TLS optional for private endpoints. We'll include cipher suite list in the security pack.
[13:10] Emma: Any known large gaps customers hit when mapping for ISO?
[13:22] Priya: Usually around change management evidence and operator separation where customers need to show stricter RBAC or dedicated infra. We help with runbooks and can provide templates.
[13:45] Samir: Can Redwood provide a SOC 3 or public attestation summary?
[13:55] Maya: We have a SOC 3 summary publicly and a SOC 2 Type II report for customers under NDA / Trust Center.
[14:10] Ruth: Legal question — will you accept our JML (joiner/mover/leaver) policy as-is or do we need to alter it to match Redwood's operational model?
[14:25] Priya: You can keep your JML, we just need to demonstrate provisioning/deprovisioning works with SCIM and logs show deprovisioning events.
[14:48] Speaker 2: (overlap) Also want note on retention — we need WORM for some records.
[15:00] Leo: We can support WORM by pushing to your archival storage with object lock.
[15:20] Emma: On the Trust Center UI, can we see which files are redacted and request unredacted versions under NDA?
[15:34] Maya: Yes, there is a request flow. We typically provide redacted artifacts by default and can grant more access after an NDA. We'll include the process link.
[16:00] Samir: For regulatory reasons, we also need to know where backups are stored. Are backups in the same region?
[16:18] Priya: Backup location is configurable in private; in hosted it's region-dependent. We'll surface backup geo-loc info in the artifact set.
[16:45] Carlos: On evidence handoff during audit, can Redwood push evidence directly to our auditor portal?
[16:58] Maya: We can provide exports and an S3/GCS push to an auditor bucket; direct integration to an auditor portal might need custom work.
[17:25] Emma: We want to test ingest path for audit logs. How heavy is that?
[17:38] Leo: Lightweight for a pilot — typical envelope is JSON lines with timestamp, event_type, principal, resource, request_id. We'll share a sample payload.
[18:05] Samir: Anything around network segmentation? We require dedicated subnets for production workloads.
[18:20] Priya: Private deployment supports dedicated subnets; we'll map our diagram to your VPC design.
[18:45] Speaker 1: (crosstalk) Are there any common surprises?
[18:55] Priya: Sometimes customers forget to scope ephemeral infra used for batch jobs; you need to ensure that control coverage includes ephemeral nodes.
[19:20] Maya: Okay, I'm going to share three artifacts: SOC 2 Type II redacted (PDF), ISO mapping doc, and the controls mapping template. I'll drop the Trust Center link in chat.
[19:40] Emma: Received, thanks.
[20:05] Samir: On remediation, can Redwood assist with evidence collection?
[20:18] Maya: Yes, we offer an evidence collection engagement as an add-on or part of enterprise onboarding. It includes runbooks and a small SE-led walkthrough.
[20:40] Carlos: For pilot, how long does it take to set up private with KMS?
[20:55] Leo: For a basic pilot environment, 2-3 weeks typical if we have network and KMS access. If there are procurement delays it can stretch.
[21:20] Emma: Any contractual language we need for BYOK?
[21:35] Maya: We'll include BYOK clauses in the enterprise addendum; Priya will flag operational requirements.
[22:00] Samir: Let's mark high risk controls — we'll send the matrix.
[22:15] Ruth: Also need the redaction policy formally for legal review.
[22:30] Maya: I'll attach the redaction policy in the Trust Center.
[22:50] Priya: One minor point: if you use on-prem HSM we sometimes need an outbound connection for key handshake, that's configurable but IT must approve firewall rules.
[23:10] Emma: We'll run that by infra.
[23:30] Maya: Anything else folks want to surface?
[23:45] Samir: Not yet — just timing. We'll coordinate on dates.
[24:05] Maya: Ok, we'll plan the KMS deep-dive after you upload the matrix. I'll follow up with calendar invites.
[24:20] Carlos: Thanks everyone.
[24:32] (meeting ends)

Note: timestamps after 24:32 indicate the substantive portion of the conversation; remaining time used for quick admin and brief one-on-one between Maya and Priya (not transcribed in detail).
